title: A Single Cloud Weighs Over a Million Pounds

scenes.text: A single cloud can weigh over a million pounds.
A typical fluffy cumulus cloud holds around 500 tonnes of water.
That's about one million one hundred thousand pounds, roughly the weight of a hundred elephants.
So why doesn't it fall? Because that water is spread into billions of tiny droplets across a space the size of a mountain.
Each droplet is so light that the warm air rising from the ground keeps it floating.
Next time you look up, remember: a hundred elephants are floating over your head.

description:
A normal fair-weather cumulus cloud holds about 500 tonnes of water, around 1.1 million pounds, the weight of 100 elephants.
It stays up because the water is spread into billions of tiny droplets held by rising warm air.
Did you expect clouds to be that heavy?
